newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK UNIONS TO STRIKE OVER ECON POLICY IN NOV.
newsitem.headline: GREEK UNIONS TO STRIKE OVER ECON POLICY IN NOV.

text.p: The president of the General Confederation of Greek workers (GSEE), Christos Polyzogopoulos, said unions will hold a 24-hour strike in the last 10 days of November to protest economic austerity policies.
The strike will take place most likely on November 28, a GSEE source told Reuters.
Polyzogopoulos spoke to reporters after meeting with National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou.
GSEE asked Papandoniou to index the income tax brackets to inflation, raise tax exemptions to 2.0 million drachmas and tax state securities to finance social policies.
He also asked the minister to pay a pensioner solidarity bonus with budget funds and come up with a realistic inflation forecast for incomes policy.

The minister pledged that no new indirect taxes will be imposed in 1997 and part of the solidarity bonus (EKAS) for pensioners will be funded by the budget implying that the balance will burden social insurance funds such as IKA, said Polyzogopoulos.
Prime Minister Costas Simitis has said that the entire EKAS bonus will be funded by the budget.
GSEE also asked the government to back active employment policies and current work place rules, he said. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
